name: Bharat Forge Ltd
title: Bharat Forge Ltd - 500493 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Analyst / Investor Meet - Outcome

summary.headline: Bharat Forge FY26 consolidated revenue rose 11% to INR 16,812 crore, but standalone revenue fell 5% to INR 8,396 crore on US and CV demand headwinds.
summary.overview: Consolidated FY26 revenue was INR 16,812 crore (up 11%) and EBITDA INR 2,921 crore (up about 6%), with consolidated net debt-to-equity at 0.41x. Standalone revenue fell about 5% YoY to INR 8,396 crore and standalone EBITDA was INR 2,312 crore (27.5% margin), though Q4 standalone revenue rose 8.5% QoQ to INR 2,260 crore on export recovery and domestic auto strength. Management is restructuring the German steel subsidiary (CDP Bharat Forge) over roughly 15-18 months, is taking an e-mobility investment write-off, and is pushing growth in aerospace, defence and JSA castings. Management guided to about 25% growth for India operations in FY27, barring geopolitical shocks.

segments.name: Standalone (auto + industrial components)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR 8,396 crore (-5% YoY) hit by North American regulatory uncertainty and US CV demand; Q4 recovered 8.5% QoQ on exports and domestic auto. Tariff cost absorbed in Q4 was about INR 12 crore.

segments.name: Defence (KSSL)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR 1,562 crore; order book close to INR 11,000 crore with stable revenue accretion expected over 3-4 years. Management expects 30-40% growth guidance from earlier call to be carried by ATAGS and CQB carbine milestones.

segments.name: Aerospace
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue about INR 400 crore; now about 26% of Q4 industrial non-auto exports and the second-largest industrial export contributor. Margins stated as above company average; target INR 1,000 crore in about 3 years.

segments.name: JSA (castings)
segments.commentary: Secured INR 292 crore of new business in FY26; growth continuing despite weak wind export demand. Raised external capital from Premji Invest to fund capacity expansion as an independent business.

segments.name: K-Drive (axles)
segments.commentary: Acquired recently; secured about INR 500 crore of new business. Management sees revenue doubling in 3-4 years, with a goal of mid-teens margins.

segments.name: Europe and US subsidiaries
segments.commentary: Europe EBITDA margin 4% and US 3.5% in FY26. German CDP steel business is being wound up via solvent liquidation, to complete around end CY27, with losses expected to fall.

guidance_outlook: FY27 India operations (standalone plus Indian subsidiaries) expected to grow close to 25%, barring further geopolitical disruption; growth to come mainly from aerospace, defence and automotive components, with aerospace growing faster than defence.
Overseas losses expected to reduce as CDP losses fall away during restructuring, with completion around end of CY27.
Capex of INR 800-850 crore over a 15-18 month period across forging, casting and products platforms.
Defence revenue to see ATAGS and CQB carbine production start in H2 FY27; large project backlog to start in H2 of this year.
Explosives facility in Andhra Pradesh: groundbreaking this month, construction by end of year, ready in under 15 months, pilot production 6-8 months later (about 24 months overall).
Data-centre orders to start contributing from Q3-Q4 FY27 and ramp up in FY28.
capex_capacity: Ongoing capex programmes across forging, casting and products platforms to total INR 800-850 crore over 15-18 months; management gave no FY28+ figure beyond this.
ATAGS initial production capacity about five guns per month; testing expected to complete in H2 FY27 before production and supplies start.
Explosives plant planned in Andhra Pradesh, subject to significant approvals; Orissa project environmental clearance still pending, expected in 2-4 months.

Acquired 30% stake in Fortuna Engineering (Nashik) for INR 130 crore; company has revenue about INR 380 crore and net cash about INR 20 crore, and plans to add new machining lines (mid-teens EBITDA/EBIT margin).
JSA capacity expansion funded by Premji Invest capital raise; plan to shift some manufacturing from Europe to India.
demand_pricing: US CV: management says outlook strong, citing aging fleet replacement and emission norms due early 2027; energy price rise a common industry issue.
India CV: demand expected to be reasonably stable as energy costs are passed along the value chain.
US passenger car market stable at about 16-16.1 million vehicles, similar to last year; Europe seen as more challenged due to prolonged war.
Energy cost is the biggest cost issue; management is negotiating compensation with customers for energy-intensive elements.
Aerospace: multiple new wins across jet engine structures and landing systems; selected as first Indian supplier of critical components by a global aerospace OEM.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 growth be broken down by defence, US CV, non-auto and domestic?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined granular split; said higher growth from aerospace, then defence, then components (auto and industrial). Outlook strong for both US and India CV.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 25% India growth is standalone versus Indian subsidiaries?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to split it; the 25% target is at overall India level, covering standalone plus Indian subsidiaries.

qa_highlights.question: Will German CDP losses disappear from operating numbers now that restructuring has started?
qa_highlights.answer: Losses go away as the entity is wound up, expected by end of CY27; restructuring is a 15-18 month process combining customer transition and solvent liquidation.

qa_highlights.question: What are the defence revenue timing and milestones from the INR 2,816 crore of new defence orders?
qa_highlights.answer: ATAGS and CQB carbine production to start H2 FY27; data-centre-related orders begin Q3-Q4 FY27 and ramp in FY28; large backlog projects in H2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Has the FY28 explosives capex been confirmed as the heavy spend year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the explosives plant in Andhra Pradesh is about 24 months from groundbreaking to pilot production, with construction starting by end-2026 after approvals.

qa_highlights.question: Why raise external capital in JSA when it could be funded internally?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the raise lets JSA grow with its own momentum, as it could become a multi-thousand-crore business, with plans to shift European casting manufacturing to India.

risks_watch: Middle East conflict and energy price spikes affecting costs, transport and demand; management says it is too early to say the worst is past.
Overseas losses (Europe EBITDA margin 4%, US 3.5%) must narrow as CDP is wound down, with completion around end CY27.
Defence revenue ramp depends on ATAGS testing completion and production start in H2 FY27; the order-book conversion timing remains open.
Explosives plant needs significant approvals; Orissa project environmental clearance still pending.
Management declined to disclose defence share of revenue, K-Drive/Fortuna-level detail, or a timeline for a possible defence listing ("will look at separately").
summary.management_tone: Confident on India growth, defence and aerospace pipeline and balance sheet strength, but cautious on energy costs, geopolitical risk and European demand. Management was evasive on segment-level FY27 growth splits, defence margins and capacity details, and declined several specific questions.
key_quotes: Barring any further geopolitical crisis and their impact on demand, we should see a close to 25% growth in our India business.
I think we have weathered the storm well and ended on a stronger note with very good momentum going into the new year.
So I don't know if I can say the worst is behind us.

growth.why: Management guides India business (standalone plus Indian subsidiaries) to grow close to 25% in FY27, led by aerospace, defence and auto components, backed by INR 4,814 crore of FY26 new business (defence INR 2,816 crore) and ATAGS production starting H2 FY27, though the explosives plant is ~24 months out and no capex or capacity figures beyond the INR 800-850 crore programme are given.
